_about: This weekend's homework (set Fri 9 Oct 2026, due Sun 11 Oct), as the two tool calls that put it on the tracker once homework mode is deployed. Step 1 banks the six questions; step 2 vets them; step 3 sets the sheet. Run from the parent's tracker chat: "Read docs/homework-seed.json and run its three steps with the tracker_exam_* tools, then show me /exam/<id>." If the sheet has already been done on paper, mark it from the photographs straight after with tracker_exam_mark_test (handed_in_on: the day she did it) — marking a set homework hands it in.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
A line has the equation y = 3x + 4

Work out y when x = 0, when x = 1, when x = 2 and when x = 5

Write each sum.

[2 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
B2 for all four values correct: 4, 7, 10, 19

B1 for two or three correct, or for all four substitutions written as sums (3 × 0 + 4 etc.) with one arithmetic slip
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet; substitution into y = mx + c, modelled on 8300/1F-style one-step items.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
A line starts at 9 when x = 0

It goes up 6 every time x goes up 1

Write the equation of the line.

The line passes through (2, 21). Check your equation with x = 2 and write the sum.

[2 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
B1 for y = 6x + 9 (accept y = 9 + 6x)

B1 for the check written as a sum: 6 × 2 + 9 = 21

A swapped equation y = 9x + 6 scores 0 for the first mark; the check mark is still available if the sum is written and the mismatch noticed
questions.model_answer_md:
Gradient 6, start value 9, so y = 6x + 9
Check: 6 × 2 + 9 = 12 + 9 = 21 ✓
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet: the Tuesday error was the gradient and the start value swapped.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
A line passes through (0, 4) and (2, 14)

Work out the gradient and write the sums you did.

Write the equation of the line.

Check it with x = 2 and write the sum.

[3 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
M1 for (14 − 4) ÷ (2 − 0) or 10 ÷ 2 seen

A1 for gradient 5 and y = 5x + 4

B1 for the check written as a sum: 5 × 2 + 4 = 14

M1 is for the gradient sum written, whatever the arithmetic
questions.model_answer_md:
Gradient = (14 − 4) ÷ (2 − 0) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5
Starts at 4 when x = 0, so y = 5x + 4
Check: 5 × 2 + 4 = 14 ✓
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet; gradient from two points with the intercept given, 8300/1H style.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
A line passes through (1, 6) and (4, 18)

Work out the gradient.

Substitute one of the points to find the start value, and write that line.

Write the equation of the line.

Check it with the other point.

[3 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
M1 for (18 − 6) ÷ (4 − 1) = 12 ÷ 3 = 4

M1 for substituting a point: 6 = 4 × 1 + c or 18 = 4 × 4 + c, leading to c = 2

A1 for y = 4x + 2 with the check 4 × 4 + 2 = 18 (or 4 × 1 + 2 = 6) written
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet; the first item where the start value is not given, 8300/1H style.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
Work out the equation of the straight line that passes through (2, 11) and (5, 17)

[3 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
M1 for (17 − 11) ÷ (5 − 2) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2

M1 for substituting a point: 11 = 2 × 2 + c, c = 7 (or 17 = 2 × 5 + c)

A1 for y = 2x + 7

No scaffold is printed: the marks are for the same three lines as the scaffolded items
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet; the unscaffolded version of item 4, as 8300/1H prints it.

questions.subject: maths
questions.question_md:
A line has the equation 2y = 8x + 6

Write it in the form y = …

Then write down its gradient and its start value (where it crosses the y-axis).

[2 marks]
questions.mark_scheme_md:
B1 for y = 4x + 3

B1 for gradient 4 and start value 3 (both needed)

y = 8x + 6 with gradient 8 and start value 6 scores 0: the whole right-hand side must be halved
questions.model_answer_md:
Divide every term by 2: y = 4x + 3
Gradient 4, crosses the y-axis at 3
questions.source_note: Written for the 9 Oct weekend sheet; rearranging into y = mx + c, 8300/1H style.

step_3_tracker_exam_schedule_test.name: Straight lines: weekend homework
step_3_tracker_exam_schedule_test.instructions:
On Tuesday the two numbers in a line's equation were getting swapped. On Thursday and Friday you got them right first time. These six questions make that stick.

On paper, by hand. No calculator and no notes.
About 25 minutes. Set a timer you can see.
Write every line of working. The marks are for the lines, not only the answer.
If one looks hard, write the gradient sum. That is always a safe first line.

Total: 15 marks. When you finish, photograph every page and give the photos to Dad.
step_3_tracker_exam_schedule_test.note: Set 9 Oct in the parent's tracker chat on the A9-A10 loose end (gradient and start value swapped on Tue 6 Oct; right first time Thu and Fri).
